claimBlocks.suggestedSection: A community describing its own priorities
claimBlocks.text: The Talimali Band presents itself as a Louisiana Apalachee descendant community and connects cultural preservation with educational outreach, research collaboration and higher-education assistance. Its public account dates nonprofit organization to 1995 and a federal recognition filing to 1996. These are the Band's own institutional statements. A filing is distinct from a recognition determination, and the pages' descriptions do not independently verify present scholarship eligibility, program outcomes or every person's ancestry.
claimBlocks.sourceLocator: Today lines 62–67; What We Do mission/history and scholarship paragraphs 66–97

claimBlocks.suggestedSection: Reading community projects with their dates
claimBlocks.text: The Talimali project page brings together an undated village-expansion plan, museum-remodelling intentions and a September 2021 account of Hurricane Ida relief. The relief notice reports supply deliveries, while the museum text invites ideas for broader exhibits. These entries show what the Band proposed or reported at different times. They do not establish that planned construction or exhibits were completed, or that old requests and activities remain current.

A 2006 History Detectives transcript records Gilmer Bennett returning from Louisiana to Mission San Luis and discussing an ancestral connection with presenter Tukufu Zuberi. Bennett describes the visit as feeling like home and helps frame the investigation's question. This is direct participation in public history, rather than a community represented only through archaeological narration. The program's conclusions remain interpretations; the exchange does not independently establish every modern lineage or a shared religious position.
claimBlocks.sourceLocator: Transcript 1, opening Bennett/Zuberi exchange; 4, closing exchange. PBS identifies Season 4 Episode 7.

inspections.method: Actual PBS episode page and original linked four-page PDF transcript opened; title/imprint identify 2006. Whole transcript actually read; no audiovisual-listening claim.

integrationNotes: Renew p17-s1 with ac17-c1 and p17-s7 with ac17-c2, preserving both original URLs. New primary transcript is ac17-c3. Do not duplicate old/new source cards or count Today and What We Do separately.
Projects remains countsTowardMinimum=false. Two substantive units plus one supporting card are the intended conservative contribution, not a mandatory three-source quota.
Apalachee and Apalachicola must not be conflated from similar spellings. This packet does not infer relationships, membership or ancestry from names alone.

The Talimali Band's Louisiana self-account is a situated descendant perspective. Community continuity and identity are not dependent on treating an application, incorporation, trademark, scholarship participation or external broadcast as a recognition determination.

Replace old multi-source prose instead of appending duplicate paragraphs. In particular, p17-s1 should not remain a generic citation for archaeological pottery facts it does not discuss; cite the independently reviewed archaeology source for those claims.

A source's sacred or ceremonial subject does not authorize republishing instructions, burial material, source images or complete dialogue. Proposed transcript synthesis concerns public participation and interpretive limits only.
Recalculate every source's full budget if overview or retained body also cites it. No Site source files, public raw transcript copy, new contacts or publication actions in this packet.
